article_content: David Hona, a 20-year-old man, will stay in jail until at least 2019 for his brutal attack on IT consultant Michael McEwen in Bondi last year. During the sentencing at Sydney District Court, Judge Penelope Hock called the assault a 'completely gratuitous act of violence' against a person who did not want to fight. Hona admitted to recklessly causing serious bodily harm and was sentenced to a minimum of four years and nine months in prison, with a maximum term of six years and nine months. Michael McEwen was left in a coma for eight days after the attack, and doctors had to remove part of his skull to save his life. Hona's actions were described as particularly despicable and cowardly by the judge. McEwen's parents, Louise and Robert McEwen, were present during the sentencing. They expressed relief at the sentence, hoping never to hear about Hona again. McEwen himself has no memory of the attack and struggled to comprehend what happened. Hona, already serving time for other matters, will not be eligible for release until March 2019.

article_content: In Houston, a federal air marshal has been placed under quarantine after an unsettling incident at Lagos airport in Nigeria. The marshal was injected with an unidentified substance from a syringe while in an unsecured public area of the terminal. Both the FBI and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) are conducting investigations into the matter. Despite the attack, the marshal managed to board United Flight 143 and arrived in Houston early on Monday morning, where he underwent medical tests. The mysterious assault occurred when the marshal was standing with fellow air marshals. An unknown assailant injected the substance into the back of his arm and then fled the scene. Although the attacker could not be found, the syringe was recovered and brought aboard the flight for testing in the United States. As a precautionary measure, the marshal was screened for the Ebola virus before being allowed to board his scheduled flight. The motive behind the attack remains unclear, and the assailant is still at large. Since U.S. federal air marshals travel incognito, it is unlikely that the attacker knew the victim was a law enforcement agent. Jon Adler, the national president of the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, emphasized the risks faced by air marshals abroad, stating, 'While there is no immediate intelligence to confirm this was a targeted attack, this is our reminder that international cowards will attempt to take sneaky lethal shots at our honorable men and women abroad.' The incident serves as a stark reminder of the dangers faced by those working in law enforcement, particularly in international settings.
translated_content: හිංසන නගරයේ ගුවන් විමානතැන් පැවැඳීමක් පසුව හිෂ්ටන් නගරය෷ ප්‍රධාන විමාන බලකැයුතුවෙකු සූදානම් කර ඇත. එය නොදැනුවත් ද්‍රව්‍යයක් සහිත සිරිංජ් එකක් හැසිරවීමෙන් පැවැඳී ඇති අතදැක්වීමකි. එහි තහවුරු කිරීම සඳහා FBI සහ CDC එකඟ කටයුතු කරනු ඇත. බලකැයුතුව යනු යන පසුව උපුටා 143 බැලීමෙන් හිෂ්ටන් පැමිණියේදී සොම්බ පරීක්ෂණ පැය ඇත. ප්‍රහාරය පැවැඳීම එය බලකැයුතු සහභාගීන් හට ඇති වේලාවේදී සිදු ඇත. නොදැනුවත් ප්‍රහාරී එක් කන්ද ඇතුළත් ප්‍රහාරය කළේ එයගෙන් පැහැදිලිය. ප්‍රහාරී සොයාගත නොහැකි වූයේ නමුත්, සිරිංජ් එක ආපසු බැලීමෙන් ජාත්‍යන්තර පරීක්ෂණය සඳහා ආණ්ඩු කරන ලදී. ආපසු බැලීමට පෙර එය Ebola වෛරසය සඳහා පරීක්ෂණය කර ඇත. ප්‍රහාරයේ හැකියාව නොදනී, ප්‍රහාරීගේ පෙනීමේ හැකියාව ඉපදී ඇත. එහෙත් ප්‍රහාරී බලකැයුතුවෙකු ලෙස පිළිගත හැකියාව ඉක්මවා ඇතැයි අසනී. ජෝන් ඇඩ්ලර්, ජාත්‍යන්තර පොලීස් අධිකාරීන්ගේ සංවිධානයේ ජාත්‍යන්තර ආණ්ඩුකාරී, බලකැයුතු සහභාගීන් අභියෝගයේ අවදානම් පැවැත්වීම පිළිබඳව 'මේ පිළිබඳ ප්‍රහාරය පිළිබඳ ප්‍රහාරයේ පරිදි කිසිදු තොරතුරු නොමැති බවට, මේ අපගේ ගෞරවයන්ට ආදරණීය ප්‍රහාරයක් වන්නේ බවට අප පැමිණී සිටිමු.' කීය. ප්‍රහාරය පිළිබඳව ලොව පොලීස් අධිකාරීන් පිළිබඳ ආතතැයි ප්‍රහාරයක් වේ.
